internal_N58_bound_anatomy.regular_case: L=n*d forces all seven live variables to have degree d=50.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.parent_families: The pivot has p=22 positive and q=28 negative parents; c=m-d=27 clauses are retained.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.signed_tail_model: Each parent tail is a vector in {OMIT,POS,NEG}^6. Opposite signs on a coordinate make a parent pair tautological; otherwise the resolvent is the compatible coordinatewise union.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.omission_marginals: For nonpivot coordinate y, parent omissions split as a_y+b_y=t_y; total T=sum_y t_y.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.support_lower: Regular incidence yields a coordinatewise upper bound on cross-polarity pairs omitting y and therefore a lower bound S >= r*p*q - floor(c*T/4).
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.output_upper: If J distinct new resolvents are represented, the representatives plus c retained clauses are bounded by Wmax_r(c+J), while unrepresented parent pairs contribute at most r each.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.collision: At J=610 and worst T=162 the output support upper is 2601 while required pair support is at least 2603, contradiction.
internal_N58_bound_anatomy.research_translation: External literature should explain/generalize this as a near-injective bipartite partial-join image-size/support-mass problem with constrained coordinate omissions.

exact_equivalent_problem_hunt.current_best_formulation: Bipartite near-injective partial-join problem on six signed coordinates.
exact_equivalent_problem_hunt.formal_objects: P subset {0,+,-}^6 with |P|=22; Q subset {0,+,-}^6 with |Q|=28; a pair is compatible iff no coordinate contains opposing nonzero signs; compatible join is coordinatewise union.
exact_equivalent_problem_hunt.output: Distinct new compatible joins after excluding retained clauses C, |C|=27.
exact_equivalent_problem_hunt.historical_danger: J>=610 among pq=616 means at least 610 pair representatives have globally distinct new outputs, so the join map is extremely close to injective on the full parent rectangle.
exact_equivalent_problem_hunt.negative_result: No primary source reviewed so far gives an exact theorem for this signed partial-join + retained-family + incidence-marginal model.

priority_findings.finding: The requested historical 25-unit local gap was already destroyed by the Algorithmist: raw_units<=3361<3364. Literature search must target independent explanation/generalization, not re-solve the obsolete local gap.

Holzman-Korner/Janzer cancellative-pair entropy uses coordinate omission fractions p_i,q_i and proves log2(|A||B|)<=sum_i[p_i h(q_i)+q_i h(p_i)]. This is the closest external structural match found to the N58 a_y,b_y,t_y omission argument. Ordinary Boolean cancellativity is not established for JANUS, so no numeric transfer is admitted.

Recovering-pair theory extends union/recovery questions to lattices and products of chains. JANUS signed coordinates form a partial join structure with incompatible +/-, not a product of chains. A faithful lattice/poset translation would be genuinely valuable; none is admitted yet.
Furedi and Frankl-Furedi give collision/size theorems for families with distinct pair unions. They attack the exact failure mode J near pq, but require unsigned uniform one-family models.

Kruskal-Katona/Katona shadow inequalities may constrain how many outputs can simultaneously occupy low-support layers, potentially sharpening a Wmax-style occupancy envelope. No signed-shadow closure premise has been established.
